question: Why does Founders Fund, Peter Thiel’s venture firm, only back start-ups that could each return the whole fund?
answer: Because venture returns follow a power law: a few winners outweigh everything else put together. In Founders Fund’s 2005 fund, Facebook alone returned more than all the other investments combined. So a start-up that can only do fairly well is not worth a place.
move: Where one win outweighs the rest, ask of each bet: could this be it?
simply: Imagine one pupil’s project wins a prize bigger than all the other prizes put together. If you could coach only a few pupils, you’d pick ones who might win that prize.
why: It changes how to judge bets wherever a few hits dominate. Many safe, middling choices can feel prudent yet guarantee missing the one outcome that pays for the rest; the useful question becomes how big each could get, not how likely each is to break even.
reference: Peter Thiel with Blake Masters, Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future (Crown Business, 2014), ch. 7, Follow the Money
